ABOUT THIS SCRIPT:

title: Manual Beam Walk Test analysis
author: Narendra Solanki (NS)
last update: 12.06.2022

This script takes the preprocessed data from the PREPROCESSOR_GENERAL_CW.R 
script and returns plots and statistical analysis as an RmD.
It can be run by itself, or used as an R child. 


INPUT DATA       : Output from PREPROCESSOR_GENERAL_CW.R (.xlsx file)
                   lookup file (.xlsx)
             
CURRENT SETTINGS : 2 Cohorts 
                   2 strains
                   ! Open Zones / Closed Zones  
                   > the open/closed zones can be adjusted in '2. LOAD DATA' 
                   
                   > This means the script is currently able to analyze a project consisting of the settings above. For all other 
                     settings the scripts needs to be adjusted accordingly


SECTIONS         :# 1.MANUAL ENTRIES
                    - In this section adjustments can be made regarding:
                        > Input file
                        > Experimental settings
                        > plots (color, theme etc.)
                        
                  
                  # 2. LOAD DATA:
                    - loads the preprocessed data and tidies it up into a polished "data" data frame
                  
                  # 3. ANALYSIS
                    3.1 Distance travelled in open and closed arms
                    3.2 Percentage time spent in open and closed arms
                    3.3 Number of entries into open/closed arms
                    
                    For each section a plot and a statistical analysis is performed
                  
                  # 4. Final conclusions and comments


NOTES             : - This script has been tested on the Project 'X'. 
                      Variations in the zone naming may lead to errors
                      > if this occurs there are two options:
                          1. Rerun the preprocessor and use the zone names as in the above project
                             ( N open, W closed, S open, E closed, center zone, S risk, N risk)
                             
                             OR
                          2. Replace the column references in this script for the analysis (line 192pp)
                          
                    - strain (from the lookup file) is currently replaced by genotype (CD1 -> wt)
                      if other strains than 'CD1' and 'tweet' are involved this will lead to an error


ISSUES To FIX     :

```{r Manual_data_loading_BW}

#here we clear the working directory again in case the script is used as a child
rm(list = ls())
#save the path to the working directory into the variable dir
dir = getwd()

#--------------------------- 1. Manual Entries -----------------------------#

# Please enter here the following variables:

# 1.1 INPUT FILES 

file_path <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/"
file_path_MR <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/"

filename_cohort_1 <- "cohort1.xlsx"

filename_cohort_2 <-  "cohort2.xlsx"

filepath_to_lookup <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/lookup.xlsx"
filepath_to_lookup_MR <- "~/6. Data from Behavioral Tests/lookup.xlsx"

# 1.2 EXPERIMENTAL SETTINGS
#2 cohorts of mice: 
#Manual setting of individual per strain and cohort, not used anywhere in the script!
Cohort_1 <- c(5,5) # Cohort 1 <- c(n mice of phenotype 1, n mice of phenotype 2)
Cohort_2 <- c(6,6) # Cohort 2 <- c(n mice of phenotype 1, n mice of phenotype 2)

# 1.3 PLOT
#here we define the colors we going to use for the different strains for the plots 
color_strain <- c("#0099CC", "#FF9900") 


#---------------------------2. LOAD DATA-----------------------------#

# Load lookup file with ID, cohort and genotype infos
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
lookup <- tryCatch(read_excel(filepath_to_lookup), # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
  #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', filepath_to_lookup, ' not found! Trying ', filepath_to_lookup_MR, ' instead.'))
  lookup <- read_excel(filepath_to_lookup_MR)
})

#make a list of strains sorted alphabetically
list_of_strains <- sort(unique(lookup$strain))
#make a list of cohorts
list_of_cohorts <- unique(lookup$cohort)


# LOAD TEST

# Load cohort 1 data
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
beam_walk_test_c1 <- tryCatch(read_excel(paste(file_path,filename_cohort_1, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_test"  ),
                   # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
                   #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', file_path, ' not found! Trying ', file_path_MR, ' instead.'))
  beam_walk_test_c1 <- read_excel(paste(file_path_MR,filename_cohort_1, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_test")
})%>%
  #add a column cohort containing ones in all rows and a column phase containing the word 'test' for all rows. Remove column 'date'.
  add_column(cohort = 1,
             phase = 'test') %>%
  dplyr::select(-date)

# Load cohort 2 data
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
beam_walk_test_c2 <- tryCatch(read_excel(paste(file_path,filename_cohort_2, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_test" ),
                   # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
                   #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', file_path, ' not found! Trying ', file_path_MR, ' instead.'))
  beam_walk_test_c2 <- read_excel(paste(file_path_MR,filename_cohort_2, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_test")
})%>%
  #add a colum cohort containing twos in all rows and a column phase containing the word 'test' for all rows. Remove column 'date'.
  add_column(cohort=2,
             phase = 'test')%>%
  dplyr::select(-date)

# Combine the two cohorts and add lookup
beam_walk_test <- bind_rows(beam_walk_test_c1, beam_walk_test_c2) %>%
  #rename animal in ID in order to join with lookup by ID and rename some columns into simpler names (replace spaces with underscores)
  rename(ID = animal,
         trial = `trial number`,
         dia_beam = `diameter beam [mm]`,
         lat_beam = `latency to traverse beam`,
         slips = `hind foot slips`) %>%
  left_join(lookup, by = c("cohort", "ID")) 


# Comments
#make a table with all rows containing comments
beam_walk_test_comments <- beam_walk_test %>%
  #select all rows which don't have na in column Comments
  filter(!is.na(comments)) %>%
  #add the listed columns for these rows
  dplyr::select(cohort, ID,strain, trial, comments) %>%
  #group the data
  group_by(cohort, ID, trial)

#LOAD TRAINING
# Load cohort 1 data
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
beam_walk_train_c1 <- tryCatch(read_excel(paste(file_path,filename_cohort_1, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_training"  ),
                   # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
                   #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', file_path, ' not found! Trying ', file_path_MR, ' instead.'))
  beam_walk_train_c1 <- read_excel(paste(file_path_MR,filename_cohort_1, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_training")
})%>%
  add_column(cohort = 1,
             #phase = 'test',
             phase = 'train') %>%
  dplyr::select(-date)

# Load cohort 2 data
#evaluate read_excel function with given filepath
beam_walk_train_c2 <- tryCatch(read_excel(paste(file_path,filename_cohort_2, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_training"  ),
                   # Process any error messages and try another filepath
                   error= function(e) {
                   #print a small message with both filepaths
  print(paste0('filepath: ', file_path, ' not found! Trying ', file_path_MR, ' instead.'))
  beam_walk_train_c2 <- read_excel(paste(file_path_MR,filename_cohort_2, sep=""), sheet="beam_walk_training")
}) %>%
  add_column(cohort=2,
             #phase = 'test',
             phase = 'train')%>%
  dplyr::select(-date)

# Combine the two cohorts and add lookup
beam_walk_train <- bind_rows(beam_walk_train_c1, beam_walk_train_c2) %>%
  rename(ID = animal,
         trial = `trial number`,
         dia_beam = `diameter beam`,
         lat_beam = `latency to traverse`) %>%
  left_join(lookup, by = c("cohort", "ID")) 

#set falling animals for beamwalk to max (1 min) and save them into a new dataframe 'beam_walk_test_keep'
beam_walk_test_keep <- beam_walk_test %>%
  #remove rows with NA values in column lat_beam
  filter(!is.na(lat_beam)) %>%
  #in column 'lat_beam' replace entries 'fall' and 'x' with "01:00" 
  mutate(lat_beam = replace(lat_beam, lat_beam=='fall' | lat_beam == 'x', "01:00"),
         
         lat_beam_minsec = ms(lat_beam)) %>% 
  # make a new column lat_beam_sec which adds up minutes and seconds from column lat_beam_minsec as seconds
  mutate(lat_beam_sec = second(lat_beam_minsec) + (minute(lat_beam_minsec)*60))

# overview of animals per cohort and strain

 n_per_cohort = beam_walk_test_keep %>%
   group_by(trial, dia_beam) %>% 
   count(cohort) 
 
 n_per_strain = beam_walk_test_keep %>% 
   group_by(trial,dia_beam,cohort) %>% 
   count(strain) 

```
## Beam Walking Test

### Experimental conditions

<!-- n cohorts of mice: -->

<!-- * Cohort 1: $n$ =  (n genotype1 and m genotype2) -->
<!-- * Cohort 2: $n$ =  (n genotype1 and m genotype2) -->

2 cohorts of mice:

* Cohort 1: $n$ =  `r n_per_cohort$n[1]` (`r n_per_strain$n[1]` `r n_per_strain$strain[1]` and `r n_per_strain$n[2]` `r n_per_strain$strain[2]`)
* Cohort 2: $n$ =  `r n_per_cohort$n[2]` (`r n_per_strain$n[3]` `r n_per_strain$strain[3]` and `r n_per_strain$n[4]` `r n_per_strain$strain[4]`)


### Results

```{r, echo=F}
make_stats <- function(DF, parameter, info_text) {
  
  #create a tibble called stats
  stats = tibble()
  
  #rename the variable of interest (parameter) with param and save this dataframe into anew variable called stat_data
  stat_data <- DF %>%
  rename(param = parameter)

  # Between strains
  #perform the wilcox_test and tidy the output into a table/tibble
  st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ strain, stat_data, paired = FALSE)) %>%
    #create some additional columns
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
         info = info_text,
         test = "between strains for both cohorts",
         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  #combine the statistics with all other statistics done within this function in stats 
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

  # Between cohorts
  #st = tidy(wilcox.test(mean_lat ~ cohort, stat_data, paired = TRUE)) %>%
  #  mutate(method = "Wilcoxon",
  #         info = info_text,
  #         test = "between cohorts for both strains",
  #         sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
  #stats = bind_rows(stats, st)


  #between strains per cohort
  #loop over cohorts 
  for (k in 1:length(list_of_cohorts)) {
      stat_data_k <- stat_data %>%
        filter(Cohort == k) 
      
      st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ Strain, stat_data_k, paired = FALSE)) %>%
        mutate(method = "Wilcoxon rank sum",
               info = info_text,
               test = paste("between strains for cohort", k),
               sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
      stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
      }
  
  
  #between cohort per strain
  #loop over strains (hard-coded for 2 strains)
  for (k in 1:length(list_of_strains)) {
      stat_data_s <- stat_data %>%
        filter(Strain == list_of_strains[k])
      st = tidy(wilcox.test(param ~ Cohort, stat_data_s), paired = TRUE) %>%
        mutate(method = "Wilcoxon signed rank",
               info = info_text,
               test = paste("between cohorts for", list_of_strains[k]),
               sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
      stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
}
return(stats)
}

```


```{r Beam_walking, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}

#PLOT Latency to cross the beam

# make a new dataframe with grouped data and calculate mean latency for each animal and each diameter 
mean_trial <- beam_walk_test_keep %>%
  group_by(cohort, strain, ID, dia_beam) %>%
  summarise(mean_lat = mean(lat_beam_sec))

#create a plot object, which does not only contain the plot but also the data and meta-information
latency_to_cross_beam <- mean_trial %>%
  mutate(#strain = factor(strain, levels = c(list_of_strains)),
         Cohort = factor(cohort, levels =c(list_of_cohorts)),
         Strain = factor(strain, levels = c(list_of_strains)),
         #Strain = as.factor(strain),
         #Cohort = as.factor(cohort),
         Diameter= factor(dia_beam, levels = sort(unique(dia_beam),decreasing = TRUE))) %>%
  #create the actual plot-environment/aesthetics
  ggplot(aes(x = Strain, y = mean_lat, color = Strain)) +
  # add a boxplot
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  #add the colors for strains
  scale_colour_manual(values = color_strain) +
  #add data-points shaped by cohort and not overlapping
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(), 
             aes(shape = Cohort), size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1,2)) +
  #define the position of the n= 
  stat_n_text(y.pos = -1) +
  # create a grid (columns) by diameter 
  facet_grid(.~Diameter) +
  #axis-titles and figure title
  labs(x="", y = "Time (sec)", title = "Average time to cross beam") +
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() + 
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) + 
  #y-axis limits (can be checked with range(mean_trial$mean_lat))
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-2, 60))

latency_to_cross_beam

```

__Figure 1.__ Beam walk test

__Statistics for Figure 1__

```{r beam_walk_stat, echo=F}

#create a tibble called stats
stats = tibble()

for(beamsize in unique(latency_to_cross_beam$data$dia_beam)){
  
  #create a temporary copy of the data with only the selected diameter in each iteration of the loop
  stats_per_beamsize <- latency_to_cross_beam$data %>%
    filter(dia_beam == beamsize)
  
  #run the make_stats function created earlier, which runs Wilcox rank sum between strains for both cohorts, same between strain for each cohort and Wilcox signed rank between cohorts for each strain and collects the result into one table
  stats_fig <- make_stats(stats_per_beamsize, "mean_lat", beamsize)
  #collect the result of each iteration of the loop (each diameter) in the prepared tibble 'stats'
  stats = bind_rows(stats, stats_fig)
  
}

#display stats 
stats %>%
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down") )

```


```{r Beam_walking2, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}

#Preparation for plot

#create/overwrite 'mean_trial' with a copy of beam_walk_test_keep
mean_trial <- beam_walk_test_keep %>%
  #remove rows with entries 'fall' or 'x' in column 'slips'
  filter(slips != 'fall') %>%
  filter(slips != 'x') %>%
  #convert remaining entries in slips to numeric
  mutate(slips = as.numeric(slips)) %>%
  #group by individuals and diameter
  group_by(cohort, strain, ID, dia_beam) %>%
  #calculate mean per individual and diameter
  summarise(mean_slip = mean(slips)) 

#check how many animals are removed by the filters above
removed1 = beam_walk_test_keep %>%
  filter(slips == 'fall')
removed2 = beam_walk_test_keep %>%
  filter(slips == 'x')
removed=rbind(removed1,removed2) %>% 
  group_by(cohort, strain, trial, dia_beam) %>% 
  count()

#PLOT hindslips
#for explanation compare to first figure

  #left_join(mean_trial, by=c('cohort','ID','dia_beam'))%>%
  mutate(#strain = factor(strain, levels = c(list_of_strains)),

         Diameter= factor(dia_beam, levels = sort(unique(dia_beam),decreasing = TRUE)),

         ) %>%
  #filter(trial == 1) %>%

  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(),

  theme_pubr() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12)) #+ 
  #scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 60))
```
